exposure: hospital-level rates of emergency caesarean section
cohort: This study included 1,131,719 singleton babies born at term in 131 hospitals in the UK National Health Service between 2015 and 2017.
finding: The study found that higher hospital-level rates of labour induction were associated with lower risks of stillbirth and need for mechanical ventilation, but there was no association between rates of emergency caesarean section and any of the outcomes.
